result.title: Preface
result.summary: The Teachers’ Retirement System of the State of Illinois issued a request for proposals for investment consulting services on January 13, 2023; responses were due February 9, 2023, at 2:00 p.m. CST. The document covers an introduction, TRS overview, required services, proposal contents and submission, evaluation, anticipated timeline, and general conditions. Appendices include vendor type verification, minimum qualifications, reference authorization, questionnaire, fee proposal, sample agreement, and TRS-contracted investment managers.

result.title: I. Introduction
result.summary: The Teachers’ Retirement System of Illinois (TRS) seeks competitive proposals from qualified firms for general investment consulting services to support prudent investment decisions. Proposals will be evaluated objectively and may lead to a services contract. TRS encourages qualified minority-, female-, disabled-, and veteran-owned firms to apply, consistent with financial and fiduciary prudence. Submitting a proposal or participating in presentations or negotiations does not obligate TRS to award a contract or reimburse costs. Proposals and related materials will be retained and may be disclosed under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act.

result.title: II. Summary Description of TRS
result.summary: Created by the Illinois General Assembly in 1939, TRS administers a public, multiple-employer pension plan providing retirement, disability, and death benefits. Membership is mandatory for eligible Illinois public school personnel outside Chicago and certain education-related state employees. As of August 31, 2022, TRS served over 434,000 members and held more than $63 billion in trust assets. It operates as a qualified plan under the Internal Revenue Code, with benefits and investments governed by Illinois Pension Code Articles 1, 16, and 20. Funding comes from members, covered employers, the state, and investment income; reports and other information are available at trsil.org. A Board oversees the System, while staff manage daily operations under an Executive Director. Offices are in Springfield and Lisle. TRS invests through external managers, consultants, and staff under applicable fiduciary laws, procurement rules, and Board policy. Fund market value was $60.66 billion on September 30, 2022; asset allocation is introduced but not shown in the excerpt.

result.title: III. Services Required
result.summary: TRS seeks one or more highly competent, ethical investment consultants to serve as fiduciaries and advise the Board, Executive Director, and staff as needed. Duties include reviewing investment policy, objectives, strategies, and portfolio structure; maintaining manager databases; developing procedures; attending meetings; coordinating with specialists; supporting risk management and implementation; and appearing before legislators. Consultants must provide ongoing asset-allocation advice, capital-market expectations, modeling, and alternatives to traditional optimization. They will support manager searches through screening, research, due diligence, and diverse-manager outreach. They must deliver quarterly and annual manager, portfolio, benchmark, peer, risk, and liquidity performance analysis, plus custom reports. Other work includes pension research, accessible research resources, proactive and requested investment education, seminars, annual strategic planning, and recommendations on software for investment, performance, portfolio, and risk analysis.

result.title: IV. Proposal Content
result.summary: Proposals must use separate indexed sections, consecutively numbered pages, and a table of contents; noncompliance, false or misleading information, or an unsigned proposal may lead to rejection, and responses are subject to verification. The signed, authorized cover letter must identify the signer’s title and include statements covering RFP compliance and offer validity through June 30, 2023; election-law business registration; absence of fraud, collusion, or improper remuneration; relevant relationships or negotiations; acceptance of Appendix F and non-negotiable state terms; fiduciary duties; possible disclosure under Illinois public-records laws; and the truth and accuracy of information, including the penalty for pension-record fraud. Proposers must return the Appendix A vendor-type form, Appendix B minimum-qualifications certification, Appendix C reference authorization, and completed Appendix D questionnaire. Fee proposals must follow Appendix D, include all costs, guarantee fees for the contract term, and may be subject to best-and-final offers. The RFP is not a contract; selection may lead to negotiations based on Appendix F and the proposal. TRS may modify terms, but state-mandated terms are non-negotiable; contractual concerns must be raised in the proposal or further consideration may be denied.

result.title: V. Submission of Proposals
result.summary: Proposals are due by 2:00 p.m. CST on February 9, 2023, and must be emailed in Adobe Acrobat format to Heidi Darow at bidsubmissions@trsil.org, with the subject “Response to Request for Proposals for Investment Consultant Services – Name of Responder.” Only email submissions are accepted; improperly labeled proposals may be rejected, and TRS is not responsible for their receipt. TRS will confirm receipt. Except as specifically requested, submissions via fax or electronic or magnetic media are not allowed. Submitted proposals become TRS property. Proposers bear all costs of preparing proposals and attending presentations or interviews, and only one proposal per individual, firm, partnership, corporation, or combination will be considered.

result.title: VI. Evaluation Process
result.summary: Proposals are first checked for all required submittals in the prescribed format; incomplete proposals are rejected. TRS staff then evaluates eligible proposals for best value, considering service understanding, approach and service quality, firm and assigned-staff qualifications, relevant success, deliverables, and cost. Fees matter but are not the primary factor, and criteria are not ranked. TRS may request information or clarification, but proposers may not otherwise revise or add to proposals after the filing deadline. Selected finalists may be invited to interviews or oral presentations (about one hour, at a location chosen by TRS) and may present credentials and program details to the Board of Trustees at a public meeting. TRS does not reimburse related expenses. Contract and fee negotiations may be required before presentations or interviews, and finalists may be asked for a best-and-final fee offer at TRS’s discretion.

result.title: VIII. General Conditions
key_items: 4. Reservation of Rights; 5. No Confidentiality; 6. Equal Opportunity
result.summary: The RFP requires proposers to respond based on their understanding rather than seek clarification; errors should be reported in writing to TRS, which may post clarifications or changes before the deadline. Proposers may not share proposal contents or contact TRS staff or Trustees except as authorized, and violations may lead to disqualification. Poor or defaulted performance may disqualify a proposer, as may a newly formed business tied to a previously non-responsible proposer if created to evade that finding. TRS may withdraw the RFP, accept or reject proposals, or waive immaterial defects; false or misleading claims or unsupported references will be rejected. The RFP creates no duty to award a contract or reimburse proposal costs, and does not prevent TRS from obtaining similar services elsewhere. Proposals and submitted materials are not confidential and may be disclosed under Illinois FOIA. TRS commits to nondiscrimination on legally protected grounds and compliance with applicable equal-opportunity laws and policies.

result.title: Appendix C: Reference Authorization Letter
result.summary: A template reference authorization letter for a prospective investment consulting firm bidding to serve the Illinois Teachers’ Retirement System. It includes placeholders for letterhead, date, reference contact details, and signature, and authorizes any person or entity to provide the System with information about the firm, its principals, employees, and agents for due diligence. A copy of the authorization is valid as an original. The letter thanks the recipient and is copied to TRS Executive Director and CIO R. Stanley Rupnik, CFA.

result.title: Appendix D: Questionnaire
result.summary: Appendix D provides the required investment-consulting RFP questionnaire, to be answered in question-and-answer order, with firm and contact details. It seeks information on registration, fiduciary duties, ownership, leadership, organization, staff, diversity, expertise, clients, proposed team, conflicts, ethics, litigation, insurance and continuity plans. It covers performance reporting, data and analytics, benchmarks, trading and transition analysis; asset-allocation research, models, assumptions, risk, liabilities, market views and liquidity stress testing; and manager databases, searches, diversity, active/passive approaches, transitions, due diligence, and public and alternative-asset capabilities, including real estate, private equity, hedge funds and other strategies. It asks about consulting services, training, special projects, policy development, public-fund challenges and data confidentiality. Firms must provide major and public-fund client lists and references. Disclosures cover 2020–2022 revenue sources, financial interests, brokerage arrangements, regulatory matters, litigation, claims, client payment-direction letters and manager compensation, with a worksheet detailing 2021–2022 TRS manager payments, products and other compensation by category.

nodes.title: General Information
nodes.summary: The RFP requests information on the firm’s investment-advisor registration, fiduciary commitment, contacts, and website; its history, ownership, structure, leadership, growth plans, staff departures, organizational chart, diversity, mission, expertise, service-quality controls, consultant workloads, staffing, skills, locations, and research resources. It asks for client experience and rosters by service, client type, and size; clients gained or lost and reasons; and biographies, roles, client relationships, and legislative experience of the proposed account team. It also covers litigation, ethics and conflicts policies, CFA Institute standards, contractual conflict and revenue disclosures, manager relationships and third-party compensation, insurance coverage, and business-continuation and disaster-recovery plans.

nodes.title: Performance Measurement and Portfolio Analytics
nodes.summary: The text requests information on performance reports, including their contents, portfolio analytics and risk coverage, GIPS compliance, delivery timing after quarter-end, customization options, fees, and when changes can be made, plus sample performance and risk/analytics reports. It asks how current manager data is obtained and whether it includes security-level detail or only market values; database size, composition, public/private fund shares, provenance, and compilation methods; and capabilities and plans for covering diverse and emerging managers. It also asks which primary and secondary peer-group universes are used and why, and requests descriptions of capabilities in securities-lending evaluation, trading-cost analysis, transition-management evaluation, and performance attribution by asset class.

nodes.title: Asset Allocation Model
nodes.summary: The text asks about the firm’s approach to advising TRS on asset allocation, including internal research, model assumptions and supporting analysis, update frequency, use of third-party research, and reliance on outside-vendor models. It seeks details on proprietary return, risk, and correlation models; capital-market expectations and optimization methods; fiduciary risk-tolerance assessment and mitigation of biases; model time horizons and responses to changing economic conditions; and recommended policy-review frequency. It also asks how client liabilities and risk are incorporated at asset-class and portfolio levels, and the firm’s views on risk allocation and budgeting. Finally, it requests perspectives on trends affecting defined benefit plans and future developments across specified asset classes, a recent topical allocation discussion, views on less-adopted asset classes, and whether the firm uses a proprietary liquidity model for plan stress testing and its characteristics.

nodes.title: Manager Search Process and Asset Allocation Implementation
nodes.summary: Requests information on the firm’s manager database, search processes (including distinct approaches for alternative assets), firm entry and fees, diversity policies and outreach, counts and asset-class breakdowns of diverse firms/managers, diversity tracking, recommendations and research. Seeks a recent public-markets search report; views on passive and active management, client manager counts, allocations, styles, performance evidence, repeat recommendations and studies; and experience with internal asset management and economically targeted or social programs. Asks about manager transitions, rebalancing, due-diligence triggers and frequency, specialty-manager capabilities, and sample reviews. Covers real estate and private equity expertise, staffing, clients, portfolio roles and structures, program design, implementation, monitoring, growth, co-investments and formal diligence reports. Also asks about hedge funds and other alternatives, including commodities, global macro, tactical allocation and real assets: their pension-portfolio roles, client use, advice, research organization, staffing, organizational chart, biographies and sample due-diligence reports.

nodes.title: General Investment Consulting Services
nodes.summary: The section requests information about the firm’s general investment consulting services, including on-site training for trustees and staff; additional strengths or specialties; fees for out-of-contract special projects; research and recommendations on alternative strategies or asset classes, including whether the firm is proactive and examples from the past three years; its role in guiding staff and the Board; capabilities to develop, implement, and modify investment guidelines and objectives, as well as custodial and brokerage policies; the three leading challenges facing public funds and advice provided to clients; and policies for protecting confidential, non-public client data.

nodes.title: General Disclosures
nodes.summary: The disclosure questionnaire asks firms to report, for 2020–2022, revenue percentages from plan-sponsor consulting, money management, services to money managers, and other services. It asks about ownership interests in money managers, broker-dealers, or other service providers; broker-dealer facilities, services, and directed-brokerage conversion ratios; and any non-routine regulatory inquiries, investment-related litigation, or insurance claims, with details. Firms must list clients issuing broker payment-direction letters and money managers providing compensation, identifying client-directed, service-related, and other non-service revenues. A worksheet requests amounts received from each TRS money manager for the years ended December 31, 2021 and 2022, including direct payments and gross directed brokerage, categorized by cash and brokerage and by payment or product type: client-directed payments, products purchased by managers, performance measurement, marketing/strategic placement, educational conferences, software, style analysis, non-product-related manager payments, and grand total.

result.title: Appendix E: Fee Proposal
key_items: A. Annual fee for full-service consulting arrangement
result.summary: TRS requests hard-dollar fee quotes for full-service consulting (including scope and additional services), quarterly performance measurement and portfolio monitoring, manager searches, asset allocation, and hourly special projects. Firms must disclose other potential service fees, such as proxy monitoring, electronic market information systems, software, and conferences. They must confirm whether neither the firm nor its employees or owners will receive direct or indirect commissions or fees arising from TRS investments, and whether related travel for Board and onsite meetings is included in the proposal.

result.title: Appendix F: Sample Agreement for Professional Services
result.summary: Appendix F provides a sample Illinois TRS agreement engaging a qualified investment consultant for performance measurement and reporting under Board direction, incorporating the agreement, attachments, 2023 RFP, and proposal. It includes placeholders for contractor details, a term ending June 30, 2028 (maximum five years, nonextendable), and an agreed-fee provision. It covers expenses, invoicing, payment, audits, records, amendments, governing law, courts, and preserved sovereign immunity. Contractor certifications and obligations address authority, eligibility, conflicts, ethics, taxes, debt, security, labor, workplace, environmental, registration, nondiscrimination, gifts, bribery, securities, lobbying/revolving-door rules, boycotts, bid-rigging, and anticompetitive conduct. Other terms address investment and tax compliance, confidentiality, disclosures, fiduciary duties, contacts, independent-contractor status, indemnity, insurance, nonexclusive services, performance reporting, audits and retention, subcontracting, assignment, notices, staff solicitation, and termination, transition, work stoppage, and payment. Deliverables are System-owned work-for-hire, with rights assigned and moral-rights claims waived.

nodes.title: (General Investment Consultant Services)
nodes.summary: Appendix F provides a sample professional-services agreement for a general investment consultant between Illinois TRS and a contractor, with placeholders for the date, contractor name, legal status, and address. It states TRS’s need for investment consulting to prudently manage trust assets, the contractor’s qualification through the RFP process, and Board approval to engage the contractor. The contractor is to provide performance measurement and reporting system services under the direction of the Board, Executive Director, Chief Investment Officer, or designee, in accordance with the agreement, attachments, January 13, 2023 RFP, and contractor’s RFP response. The term runs from execution through June 30, 2028, for no more than five years, unless terminated earlier; it cannot be extended. A compensation heading is included, but no details are provided.

nodes.title: a) [AS AGREED]
nodes.summary: The section sets the agreed fee, makes the contractor responsible for ordinary overhead and service expenses unless otherwise agreed, and governs quarterly certified invoices, supporting tax proof, payment, audit adjustments, recordkeeping, and exclusion of pre-agreement costs. Amendments require signed agreement; Illinois and applicable federal law govern, with Illinois courts and the Court of Claims as applicable, no arbitration, and sovereign immunity preserved. It includes authority, insolvency, security, eligibility, conflict, ethics, education-loan, gift-ban, bribery, securities, and State-debt certifications, plus Illinois tax, environmental, revolving-door, inducement, agent, and anticompetitive-practice requirements. Further certifications address registration, labor, workplace, boycott, bid-rigging, nondiscrimination, and business affiliations. The contractor must comply with investment, System, and tax rules; protect confidential information; make diversity, compensation, and tax disclosures; meet fiduciary duties; and report unavailable principals. Terms cover contacts, independent-contractor status, indemnity, insurance, nonexclusive services, performance and quarterly reporting, audits, retention, subcontracting, assignment, notices, staff-solicitation restrictions, and termination, transition, work stoppage, and payment. Deliverables belong to the System as work-for-hire, with rights assigned and moral-rights claims waived.

nodes.title: a) [AS AGREED] (intro)
nodes.summary: The agreed fee covers normal business overhead; contractor bears all service and meeting-related expenses, with no reimbursement unless expressly agreed. Quarterly invoices must certify compliance and allowable charges, be signed and include an SSN/FEIN; pre-July 1 services must be invoiced by July 15, and taxes require proof TRS is liable. Payment follows Illinois’s Prompt Payment Act, less prior payments, subject to audit adjustment; sound accounting records are required, and pre-execution or pre-term costs are not payable. Amendments require mutual written execution. Illinois and applicable federal law govern; disputes fall under Illinois jurisdiction, claims against the System must go to the Court of Claims, arbitration is excluded, and sovereign immunity is preserved. Parties warrant authority and valid approval. Contractor must report insolvency or bankruptcy, permitting cancellation, and follow building security rules. Contractor certifies eligibility and no known conflicts, and attests to educational-loan compliance, gift-ban and ethics compliance, no bribery conviction, and compliance with felony and securities/Sarbanes-Oxley contracting restrictions; false certifications may void the Agreement.

nodes.title: 30 ILCS 500/50-10.5.
nodes.summary: The contractor certifies it is not delinquent on State debts (or has a deferred payment plan), is eligible for State contracts, and may have the agreement voided for false certification or later noncompliance. It must collect and remit Illinois use tax. It certifies no disqualifying environmental or lead-poisoning violations and no prohibited revolving-door conduct. It must disclose actual or potential conflicts, ensure conflicted persons are not employed on the agreement, and confirm required disclosures and waivers for State officials’ interests; Teachers’ Retirement System membership is not a conflict. It has not offered or accepted inducements affecting State bids, nor used or paid unauthorized agents or contingent fees to obtain the agreement. It must report suspected collusion or other anticompetitive practices to the Illinois Attorney General and Chief Procurement Officer.

nodes.title: 30 ILCS 500/50-40, 30 ILCS 500/50-45, 30 ILCS 500/50-50.
nodes.summary: The agreement requires certifications on registration, retirement incentives, drug-free workplaces, boycotts, forced and child labor, bid rigging, nondiscrimination, discriminatory-club payments, and business affiliations and principals. The consultant must comply with investment laws, System policies and tax requirements; protect confidential information; make annual diversity and compensation disclosures; disclose compensation and tax status; accept fiduciary duties; and report principal unavailability, with replacements subject to approval. It establishes contacts, independent-contractor status, negligence-based indemnity, and standard agreement, severability, survival, precedence and execution terms. Insurance requirements include workers’ compensation and $5 million general and professional liability coverage. The agreement also covers nonexclusive services, notices, performance reviews, quarterly reports, record retention and audit access, subcontracting and assignment restrictions, applicable System policies, and a ban on soliciting or hiring TRS staff. Termination may be mutual, on 60 days’ notice, or by the System on 15 days’ notice; it sets work-stoppage, transition, cost-minimization, and payment duties. Deliverables are System-owned work-for-hire, with rights assigned and moral-rights claims waived.

nodes.title: 30 ILCS 500/50-40, 30 ILCS 500/50-45, 30 ILCS 500/50-50. (intro)
nodes.summary: The agreement requires certifications concerning business registration, early-retirement incentives, drug-free workplaces, international boycotts, forced and child labor, bid rigging, nondiscrimination, discriminatory-club payments, and disclosure of affiliates, owners, and executives. The investment consultant must follow applicable investment laws and System policies, remain tax-compliant, protect confidential information (with specified exceptions and return or destruction requirements), and make legally required diversity and investment-compensation disclosures, updated annually. It provides for a designated contact, confirms contractor personnel are not System employees, and includes entire-agreement, severability, survival, System-terms precedence, and counterpart-execution provisions. The contractor certifies its tax identity and status, accepts fiduciary duties, disclaims finder’s fees while disclosing compensation, and must notify the System if key principals cannot perform; replacements require approval and the System may terminate. The agreement also provides negligence-based indemnification, subject to Illinois law, and establishes independent-contractor status and associated employment responsibilities.

nodes.title: Insurance:
nodes.summary: Contractor must maintain statutory workers’ compensation, $5 million-per-occurrence commercial general liability, and $5 million professional liability insurance; provide policy evidence and renewals; and ensure 60 days’ notice of cancellation or material change. It must report material insurance claims, and coverage does not limit its indemnity obligations. The agreement is nonexclusive. Written notices may be delivered by specified mail, hand, courier, email, or fax methods and are effective upon receipt; either party may update its designated contact details. Failure to enforce a right is not a waiver. System investment staff annually review performance, with results presented to the Board’s Investment Committee; Contractor must also submit at least quarterly reports. Contractor and subcontractors must retain adequate records under Illinois law for three years after the later of final payment or completion, extended during audits, provide access and cooperation without charge, and take reasonable steps to ensure subcontractor compliance; inadequate records create a presumption favoring System recovery. The RFP or bid and response are incorporated, but the agreement prevails in conflicts. Invalid provisions do not affect others. Contractor may not solicit or hire TRS personnel during the agreement or for one year afterward.

nodes.title: Subcontracting and Assignment:
nodes.summary: The Agreement cannot be assigned or transferred, in whole or part, without a written amendment signed by both parties. Before using subcontractors, Contractor must notify the System in writing of each subcontractor’s name and address, the work to be performed, and anticipated payment. The Agreement’s obligations also bind subcontractors hired to perform any covered work or provide covered equipment or supplies. Contractor must comply with the System’s Third Parties Operating Policy and TRS Technology Use Policy, which will be provided to Contractor and its personnel.

nodes.title: Termination:
nodes.summary: The Agreement may be ended by mutual consent, by either party with 60 days’ written notice, or by the System in its best interests with 15 days’ written notice. After notice, Contractor must stop work except as TRS directs in writing, minimize costs and disbursements, and cooperate during transition. Contractor is paid for satisfactory work and supplies; if payment cannot be agreed, payment is based on the percentage of work completed. Contractor must promptly return payments for undelivered items. Termination does not affect obligations incurred beforehand. Contractor-created work and deliverables are work-for-hire and exclusively owned by the System; Contractor assigns related rights and waives claims, including moral rights. Confidential information remains subject to the Agreement’s confidentiality provisions. The text concludes with an execution statement and signature block.
